text.p: FAG Kugelfischer AG, the German ballbearing maker which came close to collapse three years ago, said on Friday it expected its business to grow next year, but not as fast as originally planned.
Chief executive Peter-Juergen Kreher confirmed previously announced results forecasts for this year, with turnover to rise to 2.99 billion marks ($1.9 billion) from 2.89 billion.
Operating profits should rise to 160 million marks from 136 million and net profits are projected at 100 million, allowing an unchanged dividend to be paid.

Despite expectations of growth, original plans to expand turnover to 3.7 billion marks by 1998 and boost operating profits to 250 million marks would not be met, Kreher said. He added it was not yet clear whether profits would grow in 1997.
"We are still nowhere near where we want to get to," Kreher said, adding that the company had fallen behind its recovery plans due to an economic dip in late 1995 and early 1996.

But he said Kugelfischer was well on the way to rebuilding its financial basis. Its equity/assets ratio had risen to 25 percent from 15 percent thanks to a rights issue, and bank debt had been reduced to 680 million marks from 785 million.
